text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 2.5% today, recovering sharply after a rough week that saw the stock down 4.5% through November 10th. The move tracks a significant shift in oil market sentiment: crude prices have climbed roughly $3 a barrel since early last week (from around $86–87 to $89.62 today), driven by renewed geopolitical uncertainty over Iran despite earlier Trump administration statements suggesting the conflict might resolve soon. Higher oil prices improve refining margins—the profit refiners make by turning crude into gasoline and diesel—which directly boosts earnings for a company like this.

The rebound also reflects the stock finding support after overshooting lower on brief hopes for a quick Iran deal early last week (when Brent dipped below $90). With refineries running at 95.2% capacity and crude inventories at healthy levels, the refining complex is positioned to benefit from sustained oil prices in the $89–92 range, which explains why the stock bounced hard once the geopolitical narrative shifted back toward caution.
